entries.subject: AMICA mosaic
entries.finding: Ten v-band frames now form the AMICA mosaic, using recipe-order to preserve the existing brightness reference and prefer October close-ups over distant September observations. Added 2492225173 and 2493031594 pass exact detector/DDR identity, disjoint backplane camera holdouts and sampled XYZ-to-ver128q checks under unchanged limits. The earlier eight-frame identity review is retained in the prior checked revisions. Current-pipeline sampled display-mesh coverage is 83.24% before and 84.26% after; this is neither exact planetary area nor an absolute albedo map.

entries.subject: Shape and Elevation
entries.finding: [Gaskell ver128q](https://sbnarchive.psi.edu/pds4/non_mission/gaskell.ast-itokawa.shape-model/data/vertex/ver128q.tab), derived from 775 AMICA images. Elevation is source radius minus 165 m; the original black-rock prime meridian is retained.

entries.subject: Named features
entries.finding: [IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Page/ITOKAWA/target) Itokawa centre-point export, snapshot 2026-09-11, public domain. IAU-adopted names with centre, diameter, extent and name origin; labels appear at the closest zoom only, and a selected feature stays labelled.

entries.subject: Additional October paired-exposure candidates
entries.finding: Reused the 31-product late-October header survey and decoded four additional paired-exposure geometry cubes and original FITS. Two were included above. Trials including 2495806075 or 2506694595 exceeded the existing 1.35 overlap-gain bound; their brightness calibration was not relaxed to admit them. These tested combinations do not establish that every possible mosaic containing either frame must fail.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-backed photometric treatment or another connected frame set explains their overlap brightness within its qualified limits.

entries.subject: Single-exposure and subwindow AMICA photographs
entries.finding: Inspected original detector previews of 2532629277 (single exposure, 8-bit full frame) and 2516129281 (single exposure, 16-bit subwindow). The former shows a left-side detector artifact in the raw preview. Neither preview establishes calibrated brightness or a registered surface. The current paired-exposure reader was not extended, and neither image was painted onto the mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: The native single-exposure/subwindow calibration is implemented and checked against the archive, followed by model-registration and transfer checks.

entries.subject: Native SBMT preparation comparison
entries.finding: The generic native SBMT oracle compares the full released mesh, ST_2402987304 v-band FITS and its SUM pointing. Sampled pointing, image values and visible intersections match. The UV stage reports a 1.0021-pixel maximum difference from pinhole projection, exceeding the fixed 0.25-pixel criterion. Keep this mismatch explicit; the existing controlled-DDR production route is unaffected.
entries.revisitWhen: Before using this SUM/UV route in a photographic lens, independently qualify the camera convention and account for the angular-versus-projective difference without fitting to oracle outputs.
